provisionalNotice: PROVISIONAL - do not treat as an implemented schema. The per-question field set below is a first-pass content artifact authored against the field names that ALREADY EXIST in backend/src/db.ts, plus the two tagging fields #478 requires. It is NOT the #354 'questions collection schema v2' (still open). #354 may rename, split or drop any of these fields, and this file is expected to be re-shaped when it lands. No loader, route or collection reads this file yet; nothing renders it. The SK13 pilot design referenced in Research/KST_Falmagne_and_kst_package_notes.md is not present in this repository, so no curriculum scope, concept-mapping or prerequisite-edge decision below is sourced from it.

fieldProvenance.question_id: backend/src/db.ts Question.question_id - identity convention reused verbatim. Not a questionBank questionId (that bakes in a level number, which the repo treats as an anti-pattern).
fieldProvenance.subskills: backend/src/db.ts QuestionTemplate.subskills / QuestionLogic.subskills (string[]). Array because #478 allows one question to assess more than one subskill, e.g. SK13.08 items that also regroup into SK13.07.
fieldProvenance.conceptId: backend/src/db.ts Question.conceptId. Populated ONLY where the generated skill map backend/src/data/skillLevelMap.json gives a level whose capability is a verbatim name match to the subskill (SK13.03->S4.6 'Single-Digit Addition', SK13.08->S6.5 '3-Digit Addition & Subtraction Problems'). A loose keyword resemblance is NOT enough, and a level capability's own numeric bound (e.g. L31/S3.14 'Combines Groups to 9') is a property of that level, not of the subskill. null elsewhere - see conceptIdGaps.
fieldProvenance.question: backend/src/db.ts Question.question - the stem text.
fieldProvenance.answer: backend/src/db.ts Question.answer - kept a string, matching Question, not a JSON number.
fieldProvenance.answer_type: backend/src/db.ts Question.answer_type - 'text' | 'number' | 'choice'. Every question in this set is 'number'.
fieldProvenance.difficulty: backend/src/db.ts Question.difficulty - 'easy' | 'medium' | 'hard'. NOTE: #478's worked example writes difficulty as an integer (1/2/3). That is an unexplained divergence from the existing enum and is flagged for #478 to settle.
fieldProvenance.language: #354 Identity section ('language'). Hardcoded 'en'; the repo has no second language and no translation pipeline.
fieldProvenance.version: #354 Identity section ('version'). Per-question revision counter, starting at 1.
fieldProvenance.status: #354 Moderation section lifecycle. All rows are 'draft' - none has been reviewed or approved by a human.

conceptIdGaps: SK13.01 (Combine sets) has conceptId null. It was S3.14, chosen on a name resemblance ('Combines Groups' vs 'Combine sets') that does not hold up: L31/S3.14's capability is 'Combines Groups to 9 (Object-Based, No Symbol)' at Pre-school 3, so that id carries a 'to 9' bound belonging to the level's capability text rather than to SK13.01, and it is a different stage from the rest of this set. The repository names SK13.01 only 'Combine sets', with no range stated anywhere. S4.6 and S6.5 are kept because they are verbatim capability-name matches; SK13.01 does not meet that bar.

SK13.05 (Addition within 30) has conceptId null. backend/src/data/skillLevelMap.json lists twelve levels carrying SK13 (L31/S3.14, L52/S4.6, L64/S5.4, L66/S5.6, L82/S6.5, L88/S6.11, L93/S7.2, L94/S7.3, L99/S7.8, L101/S7.10, L102/S7.11, L109/S7.18) and none of them is an 'addition within 30' outcome. The level->subskill relation is not a data field anywhere: seedCurriculumLevels.ts derives subskills per level from the level's skills, and the per-subskill REQUIRES mapping only exists in Research/micro-skill-graph/fln-micro-skill-graph.html, which is a stale 93-level research artifact. So a subskill->concept mapping cannot be derived today without inventing it.

SK13.10 (Addition word problems) has conceptId null. The only word-problem level carrying SK13 is S7.3 'Complex Multi-Digit Word Problems', which is a poor fit: the questions here are single-step and stay within 30, which is not 'complex multi-digit'. Tagging them S7.3 would assert something false, so they are left unmapped rather than mis-mapped.
None of these is a content problem. All three are the #354 question of how a question's curriculum identity relates to a subskill, and they should be settled there.
deliberateOmissions: No source_level. Question.source_level is a number; level numbers are explicitly mutable in this repo (see QuestionTemplate's own doc comment: 'Levels are insertable and re-orderable; the concept a question assesses is not') and questionBankId bakes the level into the primary key, which Research/KST_Falmagne_and_kst_package_notes.md calls out as the failure mode the 59->93 migration is trying to remove.

No stem / answerSpec. QuestionTemplate.stem and .answerSpec are marked LEGACY read-only, and backend/src/routes/questionTemplates.ts:94-96 rejects a non-empty answerSpec outright. Concrete questions with real answers belong in a question collection, not in a generation-intent template row.
No questionFamily / assessmentMode / subjectCategory / svgThemeIds. Those are QuestionTemplate render-and-delivery concerns; this set is concrete authored items, not generation intents.

No validator / tolerance / acceptedEquivalentForms. #354 lists these under 'Answer specification' and they are genuinely needed - SK13.01 '7' could be miscounted as 5+2 order-swapped, and three-digit items have plausible near-miss wrong answers. They are omitted here rather than guessed, and are the single most valuable thing #354 should add.

No numeric ceiling is asserted for SK13.01. The repository names it only 'Combine sets' (backend/src/data/skillLevelMap.json); 'to 9' is level L31/S3.14's capability text, not the subskill's definition. These six items are small-quantity combine-sets word problems chosen for accessibility, which is not a statement of the subskill's range, and no wider range is asserted in their place.
deliberateChoices: SK13.03's answers of 10 and 13 are kept deliberately. SK13.03 is 'Single-digit addition' and its level S4.6/L52 is 'Single-Digit Addition' - single-digit describes the operands, not the sum - so a total past 10 is in scope, and the overlap with SK13.05 is inherent to the two names rather than a defect in these items.

SK13.08-Q05 (128+245) and SK13.08-Q06 (176+258) keep the secondary SK13.07 tag. Both force a carry in the ones column, and Q06 also in the tens, so 'Addition with regrouping' is factually exercised rather than asserted. The array form is the multi-skill intent #478 allows, with SK13.08 as the primary skill.

questions.question: There are 3 red apples in one box and 2 yellow bananas in another box. How many fruits are there in all?
Riya has 4 pencils in her box. She puts 5 crayons in the same box. How many things are in the box now?
There are 2 cats sitting on the mat and 2 dogs sitting on the mat. How many animals are on the mat?
5 buses are parked in the school yard. 2 cars are also parked there. How many vehicles are in the school yard?
A tree has 7 red flowers on it. 2 yellow flowers are on it too. How many flowers are on the tree?
A balloon shop has 1 big balloon and 3 small balloons. How many balloons are there altogether?
Ravi has 4 red balloons. His friends give him 3 more balloons. How many balloons does Ravi have now?
A basket has 12 apples in it. The shopkeeper puts 9 oranges into the same basket. How many fruits are in the basket now?
Meena read 6 books in the morning. She read 5 more books in the evening. How many books did Meena read in the whole day?
A basket has 15 mangoes in it. The shopkeeper adds 8 more mangoes to the basket. How many mangoes are in the basket now?
There are 7 children in the first group. There are 9 children in the second group. How many children are there altogether?
Sohan had 3 pencils. His teacher gave him 4 more pencils. How many pencils does Sohan have now?
